l4_steps.name: Collect Market Demand Signals
l4_steps.input: Historical booking data, OAG traffic stats, O&D demand reports
l4_steps.output: Demand signal matrix by market/season
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥92%
l4_steps.pain_point: Demand data lags 6-8 weeks; seasonal spikes under-estimated in LF markets

l4_steps.name: Benchmark Competitor Schedules
l4_steps.input: Competitor SSIM files, OAG flight data
l4_steps.output: Competitive gap analysis by route
l4_steps.kpi: Coverage gap identified per route <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Competitor schedule changes filed late; OAG refresh lag causes stale data

l4_steps.name: Review Prior-Season Performance
l4_steps.input: Prior PDEW actuals, load factor by flight, revenue per ASM
l4_steps.output: Season performance scorecard
l4_steps.kpi: Load factor target ≥83%, yield degradation <2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Point-to-point metrics mask connection flow; no codeshare data available

l4_steps.name: Define Season Boundary Dates
l4_steps.input: IATA season schedule, slot deadlines, bank holiday calendars
l4_steps.output: Season start/end dates + IATA submission calendar
l4_steps.kpi: On-time IATA SSIM submission 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA deadlines compress planning window; US holiday variance requires manual overrides

l4_steps.name: Build Draft Flight Schedule
l4_steps.input: Demand matrix, fleet availability plan, crew contract minimums
l4_steps.output: Draft SSIM schedule file with estimated utilisation
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft utilisation ≥13 block hours/day
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual conflict resolution for shared-gate airports; SkyWORKS UI limits batch-edit

l4_steps.name: Run Network Simulation
l4_steps.input: Draft SSIM, O&D demand, fare levels
l4_steps.output: Projected PDEW, RASM, connection flows by scenario
l4_steps.kpi: RASM scenario delta <3% vs baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulation run time 4-6 hours; limits iterative testing cycles in compressed window

l4_steps.name: Optimise Fleet Assignment
l4_steps.input: Draft schedule, fleet availability, maintenance windows
l4_steps.output: Fleet assignment plan: tail type per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet conflict rate <1% of rotations
l4_steps.pain_point: Single fleet type (737 family) means AD groundings affect 100% of network simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Validate Crew Legal Compliance
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment, FAR Part 117 rest rules, union CBA minimums
l4_steps.output: Crew feasibility report; flagged violations
l4_steps.kpi: 0 FAR Part 117 violations in final schedule
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve crew positioning across 8 focus cities constrained; AWS system still stabilising post-Dec 2022 rebuild

l4_steps.name: Check Gate & Slot Availability
l4_steps.input: Draft schedule, airport slot files, gate lease agreements
l4_steps.output: Gate conflict report; slot confirmation list
l4_steps.kpi: Gate conflict resolution rate 100% before publication
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot-controlled airports (LGA, DCA, ORD) require separate coordination thread not integrated in SkyWORKS

l4_steps.name: Revenue Management Alignment Review
l4_steps.input: Draft schedule, fare basis files, historical close-in yield data
l4_steps.output: RM-approved schedule with fare class recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: Projected revenue within 2% of RM target per route
l4_steps.pain_point: Open boarding policy prevents seat-level RM; NRM implemented 2023, limited historical calibration data

l4_steps.name: Operations Control Sign-Off
l4_steps.input: Draft schedule, turn time analysis, ground time buffers
l4_steps.output: Ops-approved schedule with buffer recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: On-time performance (D0) target ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Insufficient turn buffers at focus cities during peak — root cause of Dec 2022 cascade; mandatory 15-min buffer now enforced

l4_steps.name: Execute Aircraft-Crew Co-location Cross-Check
l4_steps.input: Fleet rotation plan, crew pairing plan
l4_steps.output: Co-location validation report; flagged mismatches
l4_steps.kpi: 0 aircraft-crew mismatch at T-0
l4_steps.pain_point: This step was absent pre-Dec 2022; now mandatory. AWS ↔ SkyWORKS API integration point is highest-risk interface

l4_steps.name: Finalise SSIM File
l4_steps.input: Approved schedule, all sign-offs
l4_steps.output: Final SSIM file for submission
l4_steps.kpi: SSIM validation errors = 0
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual SSIM field corrections common; no automated SSIM validator integrated in SkyWORKS

l4_steps.name: Submit to IATA & Slot Coordinators
l4_steps.input: Final SSIM file
l4_steps.output: Confirmed slot portfolio; IATA acknowledgement
l4_steps.kpi: 100% slot confirmations received before season open
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot portal fragmentation (each airport has own portal); no single submission hub for US domestic carriers

l4_steps.name: Load Schedule to Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Final SSIM file
l4_steps.output: Live schedule in reservations system; bookable inventory open
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule load error rate <0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa load process requires 48-hour lead; any late schedule changes must go through emergency change protocol

l4_steps.name: Publish to GDS & Direct Channels
l4_steps.system: Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, Amadeus GDS, Southwest.com
l4_steps.input: Altéa live schedule
l4_steps.output: Bookable flights live across all channels
l4_steps.kpi: GDS availability sync within 4 hours of Altéa load
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS cache refresh lag causes brief price/availability discrepancies on channel-switch; SWABIZ corporate portal sync is independent step

l4_steps.name: Ingest Approved Season Schedule
l4_steps.input: Final SSIM file from NP-SP-01
l4_steps.output: Schedule loaded into SkyMAX optimisation engine
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of flights ingested without parse error
l4_steps.pain_point: SSIM format version mismatches between SkyWORKS export and SkyMAX import cause periodic re-loads

l4_steps.name: Load Fleet Availability & Maintenance Windows
l4_steps.input: Fleet register, maintenance plan, AOG reserve list
l4_steps.output: Available aircraft pool per date range
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet availability forecast accuracy ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: MRO system API to SkyMAX is custom-built and brittle; maintenance window changes often require manual SkyMAX refresh

l4_steps.name: Run Fleet Assignment Optimisation
l4_steps.input: Schedule, fleet pool, turn constraints, crew ratios
l4_steps.output: Initial fleet assignment: aircraft type per flight leg
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet utilisation ≥13 block hours/day; deadhead cost minimised
l4_steps.pain_point: Single fleet type removes payload/seat differentiation lever; optimisation is purely rotation-cost and utilisation-based

l4_steps.name: Validate Turn Time Feasibility
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment, ground time per station, gate data
l4_steps.output: Turn time feasibility report; flagged short-turns
l4_steps.kpi: 0 turns below minimum turn time (25 min domestic / 35 min focus city)
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-Dec 2022: minimum turn time floor is now hard-coded constraint. Pre-2022, planners could override — this is now blocked

l4_steps.name: Generate Tail Routing Plan
l4_steps.input: Validated fleet assignment
l4_steps.output: Day-of-week rotation plan: tail number per flight sequence
l4_steps.kpi: Tail routing feasibility 100% (no orphaned tails)
l4_steps.pain_point: 737-700 vs 737-800 capacity difference (143 vs 175) must align with demand forecast by leg — manual override common for thin markets

l4_steps.name: Cross-Check Crew-Aircraft Co-location
l4_steps.input: Tail routing plan, crew pairing plan
l4_steps.output: Co-location validation report
l4_steps.kpi: 0 crew-aircraft positional mismatches at day-start
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS ↔ SkyMAX API integration is the highest-risk interface in the planning stack; mismatch was root cause of Dec 2022 cascade

l4_steps.name: Maintenance Routing Alignment
l4_steps.input: Tail routing plan, scheduled maintenance events
l4_steps.output: Maintenance-aligned routing; tails routed through maintenance bases on correct nights
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of A-checks aligned to correct overnight station
l4_steps.pain_point: Phoenix heavy-check facility (expanded 2024) has limited line maintenance overnight slots; routing must account for bay capacity

l4_steps.name: Stress-Test with IRROP Scenarios
l4_steps.input: Tail routing plan, historical weather/ATC disruption data
l4_steps.output: IRROP resilience score; recovery playbooks per disruption type
l4_steps.kpi: Recovery plan covers top-10 disruption scenarios; recovery time <3 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Cairo AI tool provides cancellation recommendations in real IRROP but is not integrated into planning-phase stress testing

l4_steps.name: Operations Control Final Approval
l4_steps.input: Stress-tested routing plan, all validation reports
l4_steps.output: Ops-approved tail routing plan
l4_steps.kpi: 0 open conflicts at approval gate
l4_steps.pain_point: VP sign-off is a single point of failure; no documented deputy approval authority

l4_steps.name: Publish Routing to Crew & MRO Systems
l4_steps.system: SkyMAX → Crew Management System (AWS), Custom MRO System
l4_steps.input: Approved tail routing plan
l4_steps.output: Routing published to downstream systems
l4_steps.kpi: Downstream sync confirmed within 2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Publish is a multi-system broadcast; AWS and MRO system do not share a common event bus — sequential API calls, no rollback if one fails

l4_steps.name: Archive Plan & Update Capacity Model
l4_steps.input: Final routing plan, utilisation actuals from prior season
l4_steps.output: Archived rotation file; updated capacity baseline model
l4_steps.kpi: Archive latency <24 hours post-season freeze
l4_steps.pain_point: S3 data lake schema changes (12x faster processing post-AWS migration) require periodic re-mapping of archive tooling

l4_steps.name: Extract Booking & Revenue Data by Route
l4_steps.input: PNR booking records, O&D itinerary data, prior 12-month revenue history
l4_steps.output: Route-level revenue dataset by market, cabin, fare family
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction completeness ≥99% of active routes
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST O&D attribution lags 3–5 days; interline revenue excluded from base data, understating true market contribution

l4_steps.name: Pull Ancillary & Fare-Mix Revenue Data
l4_steps.input: Ancillary sales records (bags, seats, upgrades), fare-mix breakdown by RBD
l4_steps.output: Augmented revenue file including total revenue per available seat (RASK) per route
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary revenue captured per departure ≥$18 industry benchmark
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa ancillary attribution is at PNR level, not segment level; multi-leg itineraries require manual pro-ration logic

l4_steps.name: Validate O&D Data Completeness
l4_steps.input: Extracted revenue file, Altéa ancillary data
l4_steps.output: Data quality scorecard; approved dataset or rejection notice
l4_steps.kpi: Data gap rate <1% across all active routes before proceeding
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS Redshift pipeline failures during peak booking windows can delay weekly profitability cycles by 24–48 hours

l4_steps.name: Allocate Direct Operating Costs to Route
l4_steps.input: Fuel burn records, aircraft block hours, crew pay actuals by tail number
l4_steps.output: Direct cost per available seat mile (CASM-direct) per route
l4_steps.kpi: CASM-direct variance vs budget ≤2% per route
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel cost allocation by route requires tail-level tracking; charter and ferry legs inflate CASM if not excluded from scheduled service analysis

l4_steps.name: Apportion Fleet Ownership & Lease Costs
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment records, aircraft lease rates, depreciation schedules from SAP
l4_steps.output: Ownership cost per block hour allocated to each route
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet cost per block hour within ±3% of fleet plan target
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX fleet assignments change frequently intra-day; historical assignment snapshots must be reconciled against actuals to avoid double-counting

l4_steps.name: Assign Airport Fees & Ground Handling Costs
l4_steps.input: Landing fee invoices, ground handling contracts, station cost actuals
l4_steps.output: Station cost per departure allocated to each route
l4_steps.kpi: Station cost recovery rate ≥95% of contracted amounts
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS data is station-level, not route-level; multi-carrier station operations require manual apportionment by frequency share

l4_steps.name: Reconcile & Freeze Route Cost Baseline
l4_steps.input: Direct costs, ownership costs, station costs
l4_steps.output: Total CASM baseline locked for analysis; reconciliation sign-off record
l4_steps.kpi: Cost baseline reconciled within 48 hours of data extraction
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-system reconciliation between SAP, SkyMAX, and SITA AMS requires manual pivot matching; no automated three-way reconciliation tool in place

l4_steps.name: Calculate Route CASM vs RASM Spread
l4_steps.input: Frozen cost baseline, revenue dataset
l4_steps.output: Route P&L margin (RASM minus CASM) ranked by profitability decile
l4_steps.kpi: Network-average RASM–CASM spread ≥1.2¢ per ASM
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM network simulation does not natively integrate SAP cost actuals; finance data must be imported via flat-file, introducing version control risk

l4_steps.name: Benchmark Route Against Network Average
l4_steps.input: Route P&L rankings, competitor schedule and frequency data
l4_steps.output: Competitive context report: market share, frequency parity, fare premium vs peers
l4_steps.kpi: Routes with <80% of network-average margin flagged for review
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG data refresh is weekly; fast-moving competitive markets (e.g., ultra-LCC entry) may not be reflected until after analysis is complete

l4_steps.name: Segment Profitability by Season & Day-of-Week
l4_steps.input: Route P&L file, booking curve data segmented by departure date
l4_steps.output: Seasonal P&L heat map per route; peak vs off-peak contribution split
l4_steps.kpi: Seasonal margin variance identified to ±0.5¢ RASM resolution
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM seasonal demand curves are calibrated at the O&D level; thin markets with <200 weekly passengers produce statistically unreliable segmentation outputs

l4_steps.name: Flag Routes Below Profitability Threshold
l4_steps.input: Seasonal P&L heat map, network benchmark data
l4_steps.output: Watch list of underperforming routes requiring scenario modelling
l4_steps.kpi: Routes with RASM–CASM <0.5¢ or negative margin flagged within 5 business days of data freeze
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold calibration is manual; no automated trigger in SkySYM — threshold drift goes undetected between quarterly reviews

l4_steps.name: Model Frequency & Gauge Change Impact
l4_steps.input: Watch-list routes, available aircraft and slot capacity
l4_steps.output: Sensitivity analysis: RASM/CASM delta under ±1 frequency and gauge up/down scenarios
l4_steps.kpi: Scenario delta accuracy vs actuals within ±5% on prior test routes
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM gauge scenarios assume average load factor; does not model spill or recapture from competitor capacity dynamically

l4_steps.name: Test Fare Adjustment Recovery Scenarios
l4_steps.input: Route price elasticity curves, current fare ladder, competitor fares from OAG
l4_steps.output: Fare scenario P&L projections; breakeven load factor under revised fare structure
l4_steps.kpi: Projected breakeven LF improvement ≥5pp vs base case to qualify as a viable path
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM elasticity models require ≥18 months of clean booking data; newly launched routes or post-disruption markets produce unreliable elasticity estimates

l4_steps.name: Evaluate Seasonal Suspension Viability
l4_steps.input: Routes with no viable fare/frequency recovery, slot constraints, aircraft redeployment options
l4_steps.output: Suspension impact model: freed capacity redeployment value vs passenger disruption cost
l4_steps.kpi: Redeployment must yield ≥2¢ RASM improvement on receiving route to justify suspension
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX redeployment optimisation does not account for passenger goodwill cost or brand risk on thin community routes serving markets with limited alternatives

l4_steps.name: Prepare Route P&L Recommendation Report
l4_steps.input: Scenario modelling outputs, suspension analysis, competitive benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Executive route P&L report with ranked recommendations (retain/optimise/suspend) and financial impact summary
l4_steps.kpi: Report delivered within 5 business days of scenario completion
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards pull from AWS Redshift snapshots; live schedule changes in SkyWORKS during report preparation can make visuals stale before the committee meeting

l4_steps.name: Present Recommendations to Network Investment Committee
l4_steps.input: Route P&L report, scenario models, stakeholder pre-read distributed 48 hours prior
l4_steps.output: Committee decision: approve, revise, or defer each recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: ≥80% of recommendations decided in single committee session without remand
l4_steps.pain_point: Committee decisions require CFO alignment on CASM assumptions; Finance and Network Planning use different cost allocation methodologies, causing recurring meeting delays

l4_steps.name: Implement Approved Schedule Changes
l4_steps.input: Approved committee decisions, SSIM update requirements, slot availability confirmation
l4_steps.output: Updated schedule in SkyWORKS; SSIM filed to GDS and Altéa PSS
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule changes published to GDS within 72 hours of committee approval
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS to Altéa PSS schedule sync failures have occurred during peak filing periods, requiring manual reconciliation that delays booking availability

l4_steps.name: Monitor Post-Action Route Performance
l4_steps.input: Live booking data on modified routes, updated CASM actuals from SAP
l4_steps.output: 30/60/90-day performance tracking report vs projected recovery targets
l4_steps.kpi: RASM–CASM spread on modified routes trending toward target within 60 days
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM monitoring dashboards do not automatically flag when post-action routes underperform vs projection; analyst must manually compare actuals to scenario model each cycle

l4_steps.name: Extract schedule demand from seasonal network plan
l4_steps.input: Seasonal network plan, O&D demand forecasts from SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Slot demand list by airport, time window, and frequency
l4_steps.kpi: Slot demand coverage ≥95% of planned rotations
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST demand forecasts refresh every 6 weeks; demand spikes at thin O&D markets are under-modelled, causing late slot requests

l4_steps.name: Identify IATA Level 2 and Level 3 airports
l4_steps.input: Slot demand list, IATA Airport Coordination Status database
l4_steps.output: Constrained airport list with coordination level classification
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of Level 2/3 airports flagged before SCR deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA coordination status can change season-to-season; OAG updates lag IATA bulletins by up to 2 weeks

l4_steps.name: Prioritise slot request list by strategic value
l4_steps.input: Constrained airport list, route profitability ranking from SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Prioritised slot request list with must-have vs. aspirational tiers
l4_steps.kpi: Must-have slots defined for ≥100% of peak-season hub rotations
l4_steps.pain_point: No alliance membership limits bilateral swap leverage; slots must be won outright at IATA conference without partner support

l4_steps.name: Extract historical slot series from IATA CRS
l4_steps.input: Prioritised slot request list, previous season slot holdings
l4_steps.output: Historical slot series list with grandfather rights baseline
l4_steps.kpi: Grandfather rights baseline coverage ≥80% of current request list
l4_steps.pain_point: CRS historical data can misclassify series interrupted by force majeure (e.g. COVID waivers); manual review required to avoid wrongful loss of grandfather status

l4_steps.name: Validate 80/20 utilisation rule compliance per series
l4_steps.input: Historical slot series, operated flight data from previous season
l4_steps.output: Compliance report — series meeting vs. at-risk of 80/20 rule
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of series validated before IATA submission deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: Disruptions (weather, ATC, COVID waivers) can erode utilisation rates below 80%; waiver applications must be filed separately and tracked manually

l4_steps.name: File force majeure exemption for at-risk series
l4_steps.input: At-risk series list, operational disruption evidence
l4_steps.output: Exemption request messages submitted to airport coordinator
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of exemption requests filed ≥10 weeks before IATA season start
l4_steps.pain_point: Each airport coordinator has different evidence requirements and SLAs; no standardised API — submissions are email or portal-based, creating audit trail gaps

l4_steps.name: Generate SSIM SCR messages in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.input: Validated slot request list with grandfather baseline
l4_steps.output: Slot Clearance Request (SCR) messages in IATA SSIM Chapter 6 format
l4_steps.kpi: 0 SCR format errors on initial submission; 100% deadline compliance
l4_steps.pain_point: SSIM Chapter 6 format requires exact field alignment; manual overrides in SkyWORKS for non-standard time codes introduce formatting errors caught only at coordinator end

l4_steps.name: Submit SCR messages to airport coordinators
l4_steps.input: SCR messages, IATA submission portal credentials per airport
l4_steps.output: Filed slot requests with submission timestamps
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of SCRs submitted before coordinator deadline (typically 8–10 weeks pre-conference)
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA CRS portal is fragmented — some airports use national systems (ACL in UK, COHOR in France) with separate logins; deadline misses cause permanent loss of grandfather rights

l4_steps.name: Review initial slot allocation against requests
l4_steps.input: Initial slot allocation proposals from coordinators (SAL messages)
l4_steps.output: Gap analysis report — approved, partially approved, and denied slots
l4_steps.kpi: Slot attainment rate ≥90% on grandfather-protected series; ≥70% on new requests
l4_steps.pain_point: Coordinators at capacity-constrained hubs (e.g. LHR, CDG) routinely propose off-peak alternatives that are operationally infeasible for the planned rotation

l4_steps.name: Prepare negotiation brief with slot gap analysis
l4_steps.input: Gap analysis report, alternative time window options
l4_steps.output: Negotiation brief with ranked alternatives and walk-away positions
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation brief approved by VP Network Planning ≥5 days before conference
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM simulation of alternate slot combinations takes 3–6 hours for large networks; limited time between initial allocation receipt and conference date

l4_steps.name: Attend IATA scheduling conference
l4_steps.input: Negotiation brief, coordinator contact list, current allocation status
l4_steps.output: Negotiated slot agreements and conference minutes
l4_steps.kpi: ≥85% of flagged gaps addressed during conference window
l4_steps.pain_point: Carrier has no Star Alliance / oneworld / SkyTeam membership — cannot leverage partner slot pools or reciprocal swap agreements available to alliance carriers

l4_steps.name: Negotiate slot swaps with peer carriers
l4_steps.input: Remaining slot gaps post-conference, OAG competitor slot holdings
l4_steps.output: Slot swap agreements or bilateral exchange proposals
l4_steps.kpi: ≥5 beneficial swap agreements secured per season
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-alliance carrier has limited bilateral relationships; OAG data used to identify swap candidates but outreach is manual with no standardised swap marketplace

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved gaps to coordinator appeal panel
l4_steps.input: Unresolved slot gaps post-negotiation, regulatory correspondence
l4_steps.output: Formal appeal submissions; escalation decision log
l4_steps.kpi: Appeal filed within 5 business days of conference close for all critical gaps
l4_steps.pain_point: Appeal panels at slot-coordinated airports have 90-day review cycles; schedule must be provisionally published before appeal outcome, creating rework risk

l4_steps.name: Receive and parse confirmed SAL messages
l4_steps.input: Final Slot Allocation List (SAL) messages from all coordinators
l4_steps.output: Confirmed slot database by airport, date range, and time window
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of SAL messages loaded within 24 hours of receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: SAL format varies by national coordinator — UK ACL uses proprietary fields not fully mapped by IATA CRS parser; manual reconciliation required for ~12% of slots

l4_steps.name: Integrate confirmed slots into SkyWORKS schedule
l4_steps.input: Confirmed slot database, current seasonal schedule draft
l4_steps.output: Updated schedule with slot-constrained departure times
l4_steps.kpi: Zero slot-schedule mismatches in published SSIM; reconciliation completed ≤48hrs after SAL load
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS SSIM import does not auto-flag slot breaches — planners must run manual overlap check; errors propagate to GDS and PSS if undetected

l4_steps.name: Publish validated SSIM to GDS and Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Validated schedule with confirmed slots
l4_steps.output: SSIM distributed to Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, Amadeus GDS, and Altéa booking engine
l4_steps.kpi: SSIM published ≥120 days before season start; 0 slot-violation entries in distributed file
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS and GDS ingestion pipelines process SSIM sequentially; last-minute slot amendments require full re-distribution cycle, causing temporary booking inconsistencies

l4_steps.name: Monitor weekly slot utilisation during season
l4_steps.input: Operated flight records from Altéa PSS, slot holdings database
l4_steps.output: Weekly utilisation report per slot series
l4_steps.kpi: Slot utilisation ≥80% per series (IATA 80/20 rule); alert triggered at <85% as early warning
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC delays, weather diversions, and maintenance AOG events erode utilisation; real-time data from Altéa takes up to 12 hours to reflect in SkyWORKS reporting

l4_steps.name: Return or swap underutilised slots to coordinator
l4_steps.input: At-risk utilisation report, alternative operational options
l4_steps.output: Slot relinquishment or swap messages filed with coordinator
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of relinquishments filed ≥6 weeks before operation date; 0 penalty notices received
l4_steps.pain_point: Late relinquishments attract financial penalties from Level 3 coordinators; sub-80% utilisation without exemption causes loss of grandfather rights for following season

l4_steps.name: Document season performance for next-cycle planning
l4_steps.input: Final utilisation data, negotiation outcomes, exemption results
l4_steps.output: Season debrief report with slot attainment rate and recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: Debrief report published within 30 days of IATA season end
l4_steps.pain_point: Data is spread across SkyWORKS, IATA CRS, and Altéa PSS with no unified reporting layer; Tableau consolidation is manual and time-intensive
